   - the same complex pyrazolopyrimidinone/ethoxypyridyl scaffold functionalized at the aryl amino position,
   - formation of nicotinamide/anilide motifs,
   - heteroaryl amide formation involving pyridyl carbonyl partners.

","file_name":"US20150353548"},{"reactants":"Nc1cc(Cl)c(Br)cn1","products":"Nc1ncc(Br)c(Cl)c1I","solvents":"CC(=O)O.CC(C)O.O","reagents":"O=S(=O)(O)O.O=S([O-])[O-].[I].[NH4+].[NH4+].[O-][I+3]([O-])([O-])O","experiments_details":" The solution of 5-bromo-4-chloropyridin-2-amine in acetic acid (191 g, 5-bromo-4-chloropyridin-2-amine in 500 mL acetic acid) was distilled under reduced pressure at 40-60°C. to remove the solvents. Then, sulfuric acid (39.7 g, 96%-w/w, 388.9 mmol, 0.5 eq.) and iodine (76.2 g, 300.3 mmol, 0.386 eq.) were added and the temperature was adjusted to 77-83°C. At this temperature, a solution of periodic acid (50%-w/w, 54.89 g, 120.4 mmol, 0.155 eq.) was added over 2-3 h. The reaction was stirred for 2-3 h at 77-83°C. and the conversion was checked by HPLC (SM<1.0%-a/a). At 75-85°C., the reaction mixture was quenched by the addition of solid ammonium sulfite in portions of 4.53 g (0.05 eq.) until the KI/starch test was negative. Typically two portions (0.1 eq.) of ammonium sulfite were required. The end of the quench may also be seen by the absence of the purple color of iodine. Then, the reaction mixture was diluted with water (200 mL, 2.0 rel. vol., at room temperature), and the temperature was dropped to 50°C. The product was precipitated out. At 45-60°C., the pH was adjusted to 3.0-3.5 with ammonia (25%-w/w in water, about 63.6 g, 0.93 mol, 1.2 eq. needed). The neutralization was strongly exothermic. Target analysis:
- The product is an **O-alkyl ketoxime / oxime ether**, containing the key linkage: `heteroaryl-CH2-O-N=C(thiophenyl)(dichloroisothiazolyl)`.
- Major disconnections:
  1. **O–CH2 bond cleavage** gives a hydroxyimino ketone fragment plus a heteroaryl methyl electrophile/alcohol precursor.
  2. **C=N–O oxime motif** traces back to condensation of a ketone with hydroxylamine or an O-substituted hydroxylamine.
  3. The starting material contains a **trityl-protected amino heteroaryl** group; the product has the corresponding **free amino heteroaryl**, so deprotection is also involved.
- Therefore, reactions involving **oxime ether formation**, especially with the same thienyl/dichloroisothiazole ketoxime fragment, are most relevant.

reactants.name: N,N-di-Boc protected aminopyrimidine oxime ether precursor

procedure: Charge a dry reaction flask with the N,N-di-Boc protected aminopyrimidine precursor, 1.0 equivalent, and dissolve it in dichloromethane at approximately 0.10 M concentration, corresponding to 10 mL DCM per 1 mmol substrate.
Cool the solution to 0 °C under stirring.
Add trifluoroacetic acid dropwise, 20 equivalents, approximately 1.53 mL per 1 mmol substrate, maintaining the temperature near 0 °C.
After addition, stir at 0 °C for 15 minutes, then allow the mixture to warm to 25 °C and stir for 3 hours.
Monitor reaction completion by LCMS or HPLC, looking for disappearance of the bis-Boc starting material and formation of the free amine or its TFA salt.
Remove volatile solvent and excess TFA under reduced pressure at or below 35 °C.
Co-evaporate the residue with dichloromethane or toluene twice to remove residual TFA.
Dissolve or suspend the residue in dichloromethane or ethyl acetate and cautiously neutralize with saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate at 0–25 °C to pH 8–9, noting CO2 evolution.
Separate the organic layer and extract the aqueous phase with dichloromethane or ethyl acetate.
Dry the combined organic layers over sodium sulfate or magnesium sulfate, filter, and concentrate.

Purify the crude product by silica chromatography using a dichloromethane/methanol gradient containing a small amount of ammonia or by reverse-phase HPLC if needed, to afford Nc1ccnc(CO/N=C(/c2ccsc2)c2snc(Cl)c2Cl)n1.
